Git found no common commit between the two histories you’re trying to merge, so it stopped rather than combining them unexpectedly. This can happen when, for example, you’re pulling from a repository that was initialized separately from yours.

If you intended to combine them, you can allow the merge explicitly:

```bash
git pull --allow-unrelated-histories
```

Review the changes and resolve any conflicts before committing. If you didn’t expect the histories to be separate, check that you’re on the right branch and using the right remote before proceeding.
